subject: Choppy output, elevated 503s, and WebSocket timeouts during EmberTech demo - escalation
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@embertech.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, claire@embertech.com
Date: 2028-07-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo - repeated choppy output + 503 spikes

Hi Vanessa / Claire,

We started the 9AM demo for EmberTech's ingestion pipeline and saw repeated gaps in live outputs between tokens — clients are receiving short bursts of tokens (200–500ms) followed by 1–3s gaps, and a noticeable increase in 503 responses from the Redwood API. Our telemetry shows 503 rates jumped from ~0.2% baseline to ~6.8% across their region (us-west-2) during the 09:00–09:08 window. WebSocket clients also experienced disconnects with the server resetting TCP immediately after a chunked-transfer frame.

Attached are the logs we could pull quickly (embertech_live_logs_20280714.zip). Key points:
- 09:02:34–09:03:10: repeated 502/503 response bursts from proxy layer, coincident with high concurrency from EmberTech's batch of demo sessions.
- Several WebSocket resets with FIN/ACK immediately after a 0-length chunk, followed by client reconnects (reconnects succeed but output is missing for first ~1s).
- No immediate evidence of malformed input from our side; traces look like timeouts inside the serving path.

This is hitting their demo audience; they are asking for immediate help and an explanation. Can you triage urgently?

Thanks,
Samir
Customer Success, EmberTech
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, samir.patel@embertech.com, claire@embertech.com
Date: 2028-07-14T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Demo - repeated choppy output + 503 spikes (urgent)

Team — forwarding EmberTech's report. They attached live logs; Samir says the 503 rate spiked to ~7% and WebSocket clients are seeing resets and short token gaps. This is affecting an active demo audience and risks the deal. Please treat as P0.

Immediate asks:
1) Confirm whether this is proxy/backpressure (reverse proxy or our ingress) or an internal runtime/kernel stall.
2) Check model-side tail latencies, KV-cache eviction patterns, and any sudden drops in throughput on the dedicated pool serving EmberTech.
3) If a quick mitigation exists (fallback to smaller model, enable more aggressive batching window, or enable streaming heartbeat keepalive) implement it and notify me.
4) If this will take >30m to stabilize, I need an update for the customer and we should loop in execs for possible credits.

Attaching their logs here. Jonas/Marissa/Rishi — please coordinate and post findings here.

— Vanessa
Sr. Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, samir.patel@embertech.com
Date: 2028-07-14T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Demo - repeated choppy output + 503 spikes (urgent)

On Thu, Jul 14, 2028 at 9:12 AM Samir Patel <samir.patel@embertech.com> wrote:
> We started the 9AM demo ... repeated gaps in live outputs ... 503 rates jumped ... WebSocket clients experienced disconnects

Quick update from infra traces (attaching trace_snippet_embertech_0900.json):
- Ingress proxy (edge pool) shows backlog growth at 09:01:58 with concurrent inflight requests spiking 3x above baseline for ~40s. The proxy begins returning 503s when queue depth > configured soft limit.
- Downstream to runtime shows tail token latency outliers ~600–900ms for some requests; these correlate to requests that were retried by client library immediately after chunk timeouts.
- I see a handful of keepalive misses from the customer's WebSocket sessions (keepalive interval 15s, several sessions missed 1–2 keepalives in that 9:02 window).

Hypothesis: burst of concurrent demo sessions caused transient queueing at the edge; our backpressure handling is aggressively returning 503s rather than queueing or spilling to an alternate pool. Also seeing some long tail execution on the runtime path that exacerbates the queue.

Suggested immediate actions (can be done in ~10–20m):
- Temporarily raise proxy soft-queue limit and allow short drain (Jonas can push).
- Enable bfc-fallback routing for EmberTech's tenant to route new requests to a standby replica (Rishi to flip).
- Enable ephemeral keepalive pings from the edge for active WebSocket sessions to reduce perceived chunk gaps (config flag toggle).

I can take the traces and correlate specific request IDs if needed. Looking at attaching a short diff of a runbook we use.

— Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, samir.patel@embertech.com
Date: 2028-07-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Demo - repeated choppy output + 503 spikes (urgent)

Thanks — I can implement the mitigations now. Plan:
- Flip tenant routing to standby replica (standby has spare capacity) — expected effect: immediate reduction in 503s for new connections.
- Increase proxy soft-queue limit by 50% and enable short-lived additional worker threads for the affected edge cluster.
- Push a config to the streaming layer to insert a lightweight keepalive chunk every 250ms for active sessions for the next 15 minutes (aim: prevent client-visible long gaps while we stabilize).

Operational notes:
- These changes are low-risk for other tenants and reversible. I will monitor 1-minute error rate and median tail latency. If error rate does not drop below 1.0% within 12 minutes, escalate to fallback: temporarily throttle EmberTech's highest concurrency API keys to keep headroom.
- I'll also collect heap and kernel-runner stats to verify whether runtime stalls are contributing.

I'll post metrics in 8–10 minutes.

— Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, cto@redwood.ai, coo@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, samir.patel@embertech.com, claire@embertech.com
Date: 2028-07-14T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: EmberTech demo experiencing choppy outputs and elevated 503s — exec visibility requested

Executive summary:
- At 09:00 PT EmberTech ran a customer demo and reported token-level output gaps (200–500ms bursts followed by 1–3s gaps), WebSocket resets, and a 503 spike (~6.8% peak) from our API for ~6–8 minutes.
- Root cause (initial): transient ingress queueing under a concurrent-session burst + tail execution outliers in the runtime. Engineering implemented mitigations (standby replica routing, raised proxy soft-queue, keepalive injection).
- Current status: Rishi reports mitigations live at ~09:18 PT; immediate 1-minute error rate dropped from ~6.8% to 0.9% within 6 minutes. We are monitoring for reoccurrence and collecting traces for a full RCA.

Customer impact & ask:
- EmberTech was running a public demo to prospects; this materially affected the presentation. They are asking for an explanation and good will (credit).
- Please advise pre-approval for up to one month of usage credit for the impacted session and a short executive outreach (Laura — can you coordinate?).

Next steps:
- Marissa/Rishi to complete detailed RCA and post within 48 hours.
- Ops to propose a permanent change to avoid aggressive 503 behavior under short bursts (options: increased spill capacity, dynamic spill-to-standby policy, or token pacing).
- Customer comms: draft a short note acknowledging impact and summarizing mitigations; propose a follow-up meeting to review RCA.

I will keep you posted. Marking this HIGH urgency.

— Vanessa
Sr. Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
